Mydei thinks that perhaps it might not be so bad if he died alone.

“....and that's why working at the IPC really isn't as big of a deal as everyone makes it out to be,” his blind date is saying. He hasn't let Mydei get a single word in in the past twenty minutes. “You should come visit Pier Point sometime.”

“Maybe after I graduate,” he responds as he takes a sip of his wine. The worst thing about this guy isn't that he seems to like the sound of his own voice more than anything else, or that he works for that morally dubious (he's being really generous here) corporation. It's that he's been talking for so long that he's barely touched his food, prolonging this date far longer than it should be.

“Oh, you're a student?” the man asks with a raised eyebrow. Mydei wishes he would raise his fork instead.

“Getting my master’s at Veritas Prime,” Mydei clarifies before it hits him. “We were literally set up by my classmate.”

He doesn't even have the decency to look embarrassed. “You are? I just remember her saying that you were 180 centimeters. I kinda stopped listening after that, it was all I needed to hear.” 

His date winks. Blegh.

Mydei looks out into the vast galaxy through the restaurant window. Billions upon billions of lifeforms out there, and somehow he ended up on a date with this one. 

His phone buzzes, and he smiles when a familiar notification pops up on his lockscreen. The first time he's felt genuine joy tonight. 

PHAINON: Hurry up and come home, princess!  ʚ(｡˃ ᵕ ˂ )ɞ

It's additionally ironic, then, that the only man who has managed to capture his heart isn't a lifeform at all. 

“It's getting late, I have to head out now if I want to make it home before midnight.” Mydei says as he puts on his coat. “Thank you for your time, I'll get the bill on my way out.”

“I'll see you again soon?” his date asks with unwarranted confidence. 

“You will not,” he replies. “Enjoy your meal.”

If you asked Mydei what his favorite video game is, he would probably say that it's Honkai Fantasy VII, the classic turn-based RPG. A safe, predictable choice.

If you actually pressed him for a real answer, however, he would reluctantly admit that dating simulator Legends of Amphoreus: A Date with Destiny S Plus Definitive Edition is a genre-defining masterpiece that he's played all the way through more than 10 times. 

Once he's finally home in his cozy apartment right off college campus, Mydei slips into his pink chimera patterned pajamas, pours himself a cup of pomegranate milk, and lightly dabs a sheet mask on to his face before slipping under the blankets and turning on his gaming console. 

This is the best part of his nightly routine. 

Upbeat music fills the quiet, dark room, and a pastel pink title screen greets Mydei. 

He presses the start button and a handsome white-haired man winks at him. Sigh. 

One of the hundreds of wonderful features that Legends of Amphoreus has is the option to have your favorite love interest appear on the main menu, as though he's welcoming you home. 

Mydei scoffs at the wink, pretending to be embarrassed, before loading up his current save file. He's on his… Actually, he can't count how many times he's played through the Phainon route. 

Before the Legends of Amphoreus consumed him, Mydei seldom played games more than once. But there is something different about this one. He finds comfort in the repetition, and the immersive nature of this world makes it easy for him to dive in and forget about stressful things like his thesis or going on dates with sleazy IPC employees.

The recent release of the companion app for mobile devices has only exacerbated his fixation. For the low price of 20 credits per month, Mydei receives text message notifications from Phainon throughout the day. Phainon would urge him to play the game when he goes too long without loading his save file, send him morning and night greetings, remind him to eat, and discuss in-game events as though they were happening in real time. 

The entire reason he was forced to go on that date is because his classmate saw one of these texts during a lecture and was overwhelmed with pity for Mydei. No attempt to explain that he was perfectly content in his relationship with his virtual boyfriend dissuaded her from setting him up with the first single acquaintance that popped into her head. 

The game’s premise is simple: With the planet of Amphoreus and its fairytale-like setting as the backdrop, you start out as the 19-year-old Crown Princess of Castrum Kremnos and spend four years at the Royal Academy of Okhema studying, participating in various extracurricular activities, and most importantly, getting to know a colorful cast of suitors and wooing one of them into becoming your husband.

There is Caelus, your well-meaning but somewhat dimwitted classmate. The easiest way to his heart is food and joke answers that every other suitor would grimace at.

Then there is Dan Heng, the reserved student who comes from a land far from Amphoreus. To get him to open up, you must also befriend Caelus and a mysterious NPC known as the Rosy Celestial Maiden.

And for some reason, you can also date your professor Anaxagoras, who seems to prefer dromas over you even when you raise his affection to the max. 

But the cream of the crop, the man gracing the game's cover art so you know he's the real 100% canon love interest for the Kremnoan princess, is none other than Phainon of Aedes Elysiae.

Growing up in a small town out in the countryside, Phainon finds himself in Okhema after saving a noblewoman from a group of bandits. Impressed by his bravery and raw potential, Lady Aglaea takes him in and offers to pay for his studies once he comes of age. By the time he’s 21, his future as Okhema’s future military commander is practically set in stone. 

Despite his humble beginnings, Phainon is the academy's undisputed heartthrob. He's kind, gentle, doting, and makes his interest in the princess abundantly clear from the start.

Take the scene Mydei is currently playing, for example:

Year 3. Spring 15. Action Hour.

You plop down on the stairs and sigh. 

Despite all your best efforts, your father continues to hold you to impossible standards.

During his latest visit, he threatened to pull you out of the academy and marry you off to his lead advisor’s son again.

Sometimes, it feels like the memories and friendships you made here are all for naught. After all, your future has already been decided long before you came here.

“Then it’s a date, Mydeimos.”

Mydei opens the log and clicks on the speaker icon next to the last line so he can hear it a second, third, fourth time. 

Phainon's voice is filled with warmth, so sincere and tangible that Mydei can almost believe it’s real. It’s certainly more real than anything he’s received in real life. 

With the controller still in his hand, he allows that warmth to lull him into a deep and peaceful sleep.

─── ⋆⋅ ☾⋅⋆ ───

Mydei wakes up to a loud knock on his door. 

He grumbles under his breath as he blinks his heavy eyelids into consciousness. 

Hm? He fell asleep while playing the game last night, but the controller isn't in his lap and the sheet mask seems to have slipped off his face. 

He rubs his thighs together. He can't feel his chimera pajama pants anymore, only the friction of his bare skin underneath a light cotton fabric. 

And then there’s the blanket. It’s suddenly a lot heavier, and the texture is all wrong. 

Everything feels wrong. 

The sleep fog dissipates, and Mydei sits up in the strangely soft mattress with his heart pounding.

This is not his bed. This is not his room.

He looks down at his body. He’s still him, but he’s wearing a white dainty night gown and his arms are branded with red tattoos that seem to connect up to his shoulders. There is no TV, no gaming console, no glass of pomegranate milk or stacks of books borrowed from the university library for his research. 

The knocking continues.

“Princess? Are you okay?” A muffled voice calls out.

Ah, princess. 

Mydei knows this place. The royal apartments at Okhema’s most prestigious academic institution. It’s where “his” father, “his” grandfather and “their” ancestors had stayed while receiving their formal education before ascending to the throne. Students of noble lineage were granted private rooms, but only the royal family had their own exclusive wing in the dormitories. 

It’s also the main activity hub for A Date with Destiny S Plus Definitive Edition and where the player would spend most of their time throughout their playthrough. Here, they can open their inventory, change their clothes, check their relationship status with the characters, and choose how to spend their limited activity points for the day. 

Has Mydei seen that stupid menu screen so many times that he’s now hallucinating a reality where he’s inside of it? 

“You’re not still asleep, are you, Your Highness? It’s almost noon,” the muffled voice continues. Mydei stops breathing. 

It cannot be.

He nearly trips over himself as he rushes to the door. Phainon… His Phainon is right there.

Mydei’s first thought is Tall.

Phainon stands just a few centimeters over Mydei, but his figure still feels so towering and impressive compared to the sprite behind a screen. His shoulders alone nearly cover the width of the doorway. 

His eyes are a piercing blue behind a curtain of pretty, long eyelashes, and his boyishly handsome face contrasts against his sharp jawline. The Deliverer of Okhema. 

Mydei understands why he’s not real. No real human should be allowed to look like this. 

“Oh, please forgive me. I didn't mean to intrude,” Phainon stutters in uncharacteristic nervousness, tearing his gaze away from Mydei’s revealing night gown with great difficulty. A pretty, deep red spreads from his face down to his neck.

Fuck. He tries to calm himself down, but attempting to think rationally feels impossible when PHAINON OF AEDES ELYSIAE won't stop banging on his door, not only distracting him but also blocking the only available exit (that he knows of). 

Is this place similar to that planet of dreams, Penacony? One of his professors had mentioned visiting before, and emphasized how it felt indistinguishable from reality, but Mydei’s brain still refuses to accept that this could be an illusion or simulation, or even an incoherent dream. 

Not to mention, hasn't he always felt like Phainon’s voice sounded uncomfortably real? 

“Did you perhaps forget about our plans, princess? I can return another time.”

Phainon sounds understanding, but right now all Mydei can think is that he’s being unbearably overbearing.

He’s about to stomp over and tell him to fuck off when the knocking suddenly stops and the air stills. It’s as if someone hit the pause button. 

『 WELCOME TO LEGENDS OF AMPHOREUS: A DATE WITH DESTINY S PLUS DEFINITIVE EDITION 』

Blunt purple text materializes in the air alongside a snooty feminine voice that Mydei thinks he’s heard before but can't quite place.

He blinks several times. The text is still there.

『 IN THIS ROMANTIC ADVENTURE, YOU WILL OVERCOME VARIOUS CHALLENGES AS YOU SEARCH FOR LOVE AND LEARN WHAT IT REALLY MEANS TO BE A PRINCESS 』

Getting tasked with killing your loved ones one by one, only to have the game reset so you’re forced to do it all over again. Now that would be truly twisted.

The landscape is breathtaking. The ancient academy building blends well with the lush greenery of the gardens leading to the royal apartments. He allows himself a moment to admire the view and breathe in the fresh spring air.

It's time to assess the situation. A mysterious entity has trapped him in his favorite (yes, fine, it is his favorite) video game against his will. There are no viable methods of escape. What awaits him back in the real world is endless schoolwork and an empty apartment. His only task is to flirt and go on silly little dates with the fictional character he's been in a parasocial relationship with for the better half of the year.

If there is anything Mydeimos prides himself in, it’s his ability to adapt to any situation. 

And when he really thinks about it, is his predicament really all that bad?

Instead of mulling over it, he decides that he should no longer keep Phainon waiting.

Each one of the suitors has a preferred clothing style for the princess that the player can follow to score additional affection points during dates. As he represents the clean-cut, boy next door archetype, Phainon's preference obviously leaned towards the Natural style.

It's not Mydei's favorite, but it's not his personal preferences that will carry him through a perfect playthrough, so he sucks it up.

One thing Mydei appreciates about Legends of Amphoreus: A Date with Destiny S Plus Definitive Edition is that the Crown Princess of Castrum Kremnos is canonically beautiful. The first time Mydei heard this line, he swore under his breath before burying his face in his pillow and screaming.

“You really didn't have to…” Mydei forces a pout. 

“Precious gemstones go through a long and arduous process of refinement before they’re deemed suitable for sale,” Phainon continues his corny romantic spiel. Mydei listens intently anyway, it feels like he’s watching a live reenactment of his favorite game. “But their brilliant color, the essence of their beauty, is present through all these stages. To the right person, a precious gemstone is always just that… precious.”

“I am most relieved to hear it,” Phainon replies softly, resting a hand on his chest. 

His town square date revolves around doting on the princess. 

The walk back to the academy is quiet. The sun is setting, and Phainon is humming something that vaguely resembles a Kremnoan folk song. Mydei’s heart aches for a home that he’s never been to.

It all feels a little like those late nights where he leaves the game running mid-dialogue and lets Phainon blink at him behind the screen. His presence alone is comfortable and familiar, offering the companionship Mydei had been yearning for.

He’d close his eyes sometimes and picture Phainon at his side, holding Mydei’s waist and nuzzling his face into his neck as he reads the dialogue out loud and teases him about his choices. 

When he fell asleep last night, he’d pictured himself in Phainon’s arms. 

It’s easier for Mydei to admit now, but the knowledge that he can never feel Phainon’s body against his has always hurt. It felt like he was constantly mourning a lover who never even had the chance to live.

That feeling claws at him as they stand outside the royal apartment, and as every single cell in his body screams for him to tell Phainon to stay with him, Mydei gives in. 

As long as Phainon exists in front of him now, as real as any human can be, Mydei will take every opportunity to fulfill the intimate fantasies that had left him frustrated and lonely all these months. What is Purple Voice going to do about it? He’s just fulfilling his task of winning Phainon over, and the cheesy PG-rated lines about how he’s like an earring isn’t going to cut it. 

“I was honored to have those few hours of your time to myself, Mydeimos,” Phainon says with a perfectly practiced bow. “I hope I offered you some comfort during the brief moments we have together.” 

It’s always about me, never you.

Feeling impatient, Mydei parts his lips and tugs on Phainon’s shirt to bring him closer. 

Phainon’s entire demeanor shifts. His body goes stiff, and his courteous smile falls. He doesn't move. 

He’s looking at Mydei’s lips.

But Phainon’s smile returns, and his blue eyes grow cold and distant. 

He takes a step back, a polite but straightforward rejection towards Mydei’s off-script advances. 

To add insult to injury, he consoles Mydei with a light head pat. 

“You had a long day. Rest well, Your Highness.”

Because we’re friends. Because I care for you. Because you’re the Kremnoan Princess and I’m Phainon of Aedes Elysiae and this is our preordained fate. 

“Because you’re acting strange,” Phainon answers coldly. “I’m curious to know what’s wrong.”

Mydei spares him a look then, and the experienced fighter part of his brain instinctively registers the concerned hand Phainon was about to place on his shoulder as an ambush attack. 

He slaps Phainon’s arm away the way he would an opponent in a fight ring.

They stare at each other, the air between them so still Mydei expects Purple Voice to appear and scold him at any moment. 

Instead of demanding to know why Mydei just did that, Phainon tries to touch him again, like he’s attempting to taste a forbidden fruit. 

And that’s exactly what Mydei gives him, because he gets light on his feet and twists his body to dodge his advance perfectly. 

Phainon hums and shrugs off the invisible shackles that had been holding him back from using his full strength on Mydei. 

He comes at him with punches and kicks that could render the average man unconscious, all of which Mydei intercepts or tanks with ease.

It’s not hard for Mydei to understand. He wouldn’t resist the temptation of battling an even opponent either. Their battle additionally feels like an outlet for all the frustration and heartbreak that Phainon has put him through.

They spar for a while, and Mydei thinks that they could go for hours until he hears fabric rip around his hips, baring a few centimeters of his ass. Phainon’s attention is diverted in an instant to steal a look, and his split second distraction provides Mydei an opening to overpower him.

He sends him falling on to the grass, and with most of his strength depleted, Mydei lands on top of Phainon, his bare thighs straddling his waist.

If Phainon was apathetic before, he must truly despise him now. Mydei didn’t want to show this side of him here, he was content playing a role that he never quite fit in so he could continue enjoying Phainon’s unwavering affection for the princess.

“You stupid Deliverer,” Mydei pounds on Phainon’s chest, tears stinging his eyes and blurring his vision. Fuck Figstew, fuck the academy, fuck this world and what it’s done to his Phainon. “Why won’t you just like me? Am I not good enough for you?”

He sniffs, his chest feeling heavier with every breath he takes, and he braces himself for a system reset that doesn’t come. 

Phainon smiles. 

Actually, really smiles. None of that polite, polished bullshit. It’s a little crooked, accompanied by a lively but mischievous spark in his eyes. 

“You’ve never looked as beautiful as you do in this moment, Mydeimos.”

“I’m trying to get my head around this.” Mydei, for some reason, still tries to talk things out with Figstew. He’s sitting cross-legged on his bed across from the spawn of Nanook. “Phainon likes it when I hit him?”

“Player Mydeimos has made significant progress,” Figstew answers, or rather, doesn’t answer his question at all. There is something strange about it tonight, namely the faint spark of joy flashing across its lifeless eyes. “All thanks to the help of his trusty Figstew!”

“Help, my ass! You broke my Deliverer and now he gets off on being punched in the face!”

Figstew does a big stretch, spreading its little paws in Mydei’s face. It’s almost cute. “The game files have not been altered. The system is currently running the latest version and does not require any further updates.”

“Are you sure? Have you tried turning him on and off?”

“A system reboot is only performed at the event of an emergency,” Figstew replies, which sort of implies that Phainon can be turned on and off. Unfortunately, Mydei only knows how to do the former.

Fifty percent. Fifty fucking percent. Weeks of pointless suffering and all it took for Phainon to come around was Mydei getting physical with him in the most literal sense. 

Despite berating his fluffy captor, Mydei knows deep down that there is nothing wrong with Phainon, or at least not with this version of him. All his actions leading to the festival made it clear that he’s been hiding something all along. Mydei had felt the sting of his polite indifference and caught the fleeting glimpses into something cold and angry behind his eyes, but it’s only when he came face to face with the true Phainon that he realized just how big the distance between them had been. 

Immediately after their match, Phainon escorted Mydei back to his room, correctly deducing that the princess is in no shape to be seen in public, what with his dirt covered ripped dress, tear stained face, and bird nest shaped hair. 

Mydei could only will himself to stop crying once he was alone again.

Even though he’s finally succeeded, Mydei can’t enjoy the taste of this hollow victory. He’s emotionally drained, and all he feels is confusion and deeper alienation. The man he thought he knew like the back of his hand is as good as a stranger.

And what is it exactly that forced Phainon out of his shell? Is it the simple thrill of battle? Does he think crying is sexy? Is it that stupid revealing dress?

Does Phainon just like Mydei’s actual personality?

He scoffs at the last one. Phainon barely knows anything about him, so it wouldn’t make any sense.

Mydei’s train of thoughts is abruptly cut short when Figstew leaps into his chest, and the sheer force of its weight sends him falling on his back, with his head conveniently dropping on the pillow. 

“You are exhausted, Player Mydeimos,” it scolds him before using its mouth to pull the blanket over Mydei’s body. “You’re going to need ample rest if you want to meet your objective.”

Okay. Maybe he’s not so alone.

Year 3. Spring 34. Entry Hour.

╰── ⋅ ⋅ ── ✩ ── ⋅ ⋅ ──╯

For the first time since he arrived in Amphoreus, Mydei wakes up and thinks about what he actually wants to do, and not what he should be doing.

Their classes won’t resume for another day, which means that he gets an entire day to collect his thoughts and take a breather.

The academy's training grounds are technically open for all students to use, but it’s not a place the princess is ever seen in during Phainon’s playthroughs because big muscles aren't exactly to his taste. 

Well, that doesn’t matter to Mydei now. Because everything that he knew to be true is apparently a lie, and because he earned a break from playing Phainon’s perfect little princess.

The grounds are empty when Mydei arrives just after dawn, so quiet you could hear a pin drop, and a deep sense of relief washes over him. It’s the first time he’s been able to feel like himself outside the confines of the royal apartments. 

He scans over the available weapons, all of which fit into the fairytale fantasy setting. He tries swords, axes, spears, before landing on a pair of heavy rose gold gauntlets. 

Surprisingly, they fit him perfectly, and Mydei smiles as he flexes his fingers. He’s always been partial to hand to hand combat.

With a stupid, infuriating Deliverer at the back of his mind, he throws a test paunch in the air. 

“You could try those on me, if you’d like,” Phainon says from behind him. 

Of course.

The only person crazy enough to choose training at the break of dawn on a holiday is none other than the phantom Mydei was directing his punches to.

“You’re up early,” Mydei notes instead of pretending to blush and stutter through a good morning. It feels so good to finally abandon that exhausting act.

Phainon’s default smile turns slightly manic at Mydei’s aloof response. “Well, I have to work hard to make up for my crushing defeat yesterday don’t I?”

“Crushing is a bit of an exaggeration. Give yourself some credit,” Mydei scoffs. 

“I’ll take your word for it,” Phainon agrees easily. “I’m just surprised the princess has secretly been a master of martial arts all along. You’re the first person to ever stand a chance against me since I arrived in Okhema.”

He says those words not with contempt or surprise, but with utter reverence and adoration. The simple idea of Mydei matching, or even surpassing him in battle fills Phainon’s voice with glee and excitement that Mydei has never heard in hundreds, if not thousands of voiced dialogue lines.

The shift is so jarring that he almost forgets that he needs to have an explanation as to why he’s been hiding these skills, and how he developed them in the first place.

Mydei chooses to tell the truth, or at least some version of it.

“I've been fighting ever since I can remember,” he starts to explain. His parents were professional fighters and had won tournaments across the galaxy before finally facing each other in battle. Mydei was born not long after. “In every discipline you could think of. It was part of my training as a Kremnoan royal.”

His parents had encouraged him to take the same path, but despite his talent, Mydei was turned off by the violent and corrupt nature of the industry and turned to his studies instead.

He liked to fight. He didn’t like doing it for a living.

“We’ve known each other for years now, but you’ve kept those talents well hidden from me,” Phainon says. His voice is still light, but the undercurrent of suspicion is clear as day. He’s sharper than Mydei had assumed. 

“I suppose I’m better than the average Okheman grunt,” Mydei can’t help but quip, and Phainon laughs. “But I don’t like to contribute to senseless violence. The less I have to use my fists, the better.”

Phainon seems satisfied with this answer, and he nods to himself thoughtfully before making a proposal. “Considering the fact that you’re here, I suppose a few rounds of friendly sparring is not off limits?”

Mydei stares at him in disbelief. He’s ridiculous. The princess he’s been courting for three years, doted on and obsessed over every single day, has suddenly revealed this deadly talent, and his first response is to test it with his own body instead of fearing for his life.

“Only if you can keep up,” Mydei says, deciding to throw him a bone. Phainon looks like he’s about to piss himself with excitement. 

They spend the morning fighting, and Mydei doesn’t have the advantage of skimpy clothing anymore, while Phainon proves to be a lot more fearsome early in the morning after he’s had a good night’s rest.

Phainon ends up winning a best of five match, and they both lay on the ground afterwards, their shallow breathing synchronized. It’s the most that Mydei has felt like himself in weeks, and it’s nothing short of exhilarating. 

“Hey princess.”

“Yes, Deliverer?”

“I do like you,” Phainon says in a saccharine tone, just a notch above his standard, corny romantic lines. “You are good enough for me, princess.”

Oh.

Phainon is making fun of him.

“Fuck off!” Mydei snarls and kicks him with all his might, his face suddenly burning up. He never even imagined that Phainon was capable of snark, and was banking on him being too polite to mention Mydei’s embarrassing outburst and hurt his pride. “I was just tired yesterday, I wasn’t thinking about what I was saying.”

Phainon rolls over with a hearty laugh.

A week ago, he would have been deathly afraid of making any indication that he might not return Phainon’s feelings (which he had been doubting even existed) will blow the entire universe up and leave him trapped with Figstew forever. But his flustered, ugly, violent response only seems to lift Phainon’s spirits up.

The Deliverer is deeply unwell. 

“I’m going to get something to eat,” Mydei grumbles, standing up. So much for his quiet day off.

“Let’s go together?” Phainon suggests immediately.

The inquisitive, academic side of Mydei wonders how much meaner he can be, how far he can try to push Phainon away, literally and figuratively, before he decides it’s too much. 

“No,” he replies, not just to see what happens but also because the entire reason he woke up early today was to spend time alone.

“Please, princess,” Phainon pleads without a shred of hesitation or dignity. Mydei thinks Lady Aglaea would have a heart attack watching the result of her careful upbringing fall apart so easily. 

Mydei wants to say no again, but Phainon’s stupid blue eyes are stupidly big and stupidly pathetic and stupidly endearing. 

Despite how irritated he’s been, Mydei’s heart still belongs to Phainon. 

Before he knows it, he’s in the dining hall at breakfast time, the Deliverer sitting next to him instead of across the table like their usual dates. Mydei might just be feeling disoriented, but he could swear that their chairs are much closer than they should be.

Phainon has barely touched his food, opting instead to watch Mydei eat with an unreadable expression. 

I feel full just watching you eat, princess, was one of his default lines. It’s the first time Mydei has felt like he actually means it, even without saying a single word. 

“Hey princess,” he calls with a hush, and Mydei mourns the momentary peace he was enjoying. “Between the two of us, who do you think is actually stronger?”

Of course he’d only ask that after he defeated Mydei three times in a row. 

“Is it really wise for an Okheman soldier to pose this question to the heir to the Kremnoan throne?” Mydei answers diplomatically, barely resisting the bait. 

“Hmm, I wouldn't describe your ambush yesterday as wise either,” Phainon answers darkly. Fucking asshole. “So let’s just say that matters of courtesy no longer exist between us, okay?”

Mydei doesn't know what to say in return. It’s all a little scary, if he’s being honest. It feels like he’s conversing with a stranger wearing a familiar skin. Phainon is as charming as ever, except he’s now bared his fangs. They're sharp and lethal, and worst of all, impossible for Mydei to fully make sense of. 

He must be just as unwell, because he’s also never felt more attracted to Phainon. 

“Whatever,” he mutters as he looks away, his face warm. 

“Unlesssss,” Phainon adds. “Princess Mydeimos is too proud to admit that I’m clearly superior?” 

Mydei should legally be allowed to kill him. It probably is permissible under Kremnoan law.

“You asshole,” he curses under his breath, grabbing Phainon’s face in his hand. Phainon’s eyes widen, and he smiles like Mydei just professed his love for him. “Don’t be stupid. You only got an edge over me because you train every single day, and just barely at that.” 

His outburst attracts the attention of the few students around them, and he releases Phainon immediately, more angry at himself for allowing such easy bait to rile him up. 

Phainon is still beaming though, which Mydei supposes falls under his objective, but it gives him no joy or sense of accomplishment.

“It sounds like you have no choice but to join me for training every morning then,” Phainon replies with a shrug, happily rubbing his cheeks, now bearing red streaks from the pressure of Mydei’s hand. 

It’s a tempting offer. Going so many weeks without his morning gym sessions has been unbearable, and he gets to spend time with Phainon on top of that. 

“I’ll come by if I feel like it, but you better not distract me,” Mydei warns. 

He goes silent for a bit, and then decides that they’ve broken so many boundaries already. He allows himself one honest question. “What has gotten into you, Lord Phainon?”

Does it count as breaking the fourth wall for him to ask? Does the game register Phainon’s new personality to have always been a part of him, just like it reads the princess to have always been a 185cm hunk with arms the size of the original protagonist’s waist?

“It's just that I’ve realized something crucial about His Highness,” Phainon clears away these doubts in an instant. So they’ve both felt that shift. Well, as much as a bundle of pixels can feel anyway. 

“And that is?”

“You’re extremely cute when you get angry,” Phainon admits, a little hesitantly. It’s a little funny because he’s made his intentions crystal clear through his actions, but it’s only when he’s cornered into properly verbalizing them that he struggles with honesty. 

Mydei sees it in his eyes then. 

Phainon is scared. He’s scared he would do something and force Mydei’s true self back into hiding. Mydei knows exactly how he feels. It’s the same torture he’s experienced since he arrived.

“You’re an idiot,” he responds, rolling his eyes. 

Phainon, who has already come to understand this response as a friendly gesture, breathes a sigh of relief.

Mydei has a chilling realization once he returns to his room.

Phainon hasn't said a single scripted line today.

Year 3. Spring 38. Ascent Hour.

╰── ⋅ ⋅ ── ✩ ── ⋅ ⋅ ──╯

It’s like Phainon has tied an invisible leash around Mydei’s neck.

“I don’t need to be escorted to every class, Deliverer,” he grumbles. 

Phainon and Mydei have been inseparable since the Festival of Flowers, and not through any effort from Mydei. The moment he leaves his apartment, Phainon would squeeze himself into every possible part of his day.

It’s not exactly difficult. They had most of the same classes, Phainon was eligible to join him for every meal (although the game’s randomized coding normally prevented Mydei from eating with the same person every single day), and Mydei now has access to the training grounds in the morning before class.

If Mydei said no, he would insist. If he got a little mean, Phainon’s affection would only go up.

“Come on, Mydeimos.” Phainon has been calling him that more often lately. Using the princess’ given name is normally reserved for special occasions, especially with Phainon, whose whole thing is knightly chivalry and old school courting. 

This is what he’s yearned for in real life, isn't it? For Phainon to dote on him around the clock? 

Well, not exactly. The issue is that Phainon doesn't hold his hand and sweetly asks him about his day. No, he has an um, more unique approach to providing Mydei with his undivided attention. 

“Do you want to race to the next class? Surely you can't also be faster than me.” 

“I’m not going to sprint in this dress, especially not in front of my future subjects,” Mydei grits his teeth. The unwanted attention from the NPCs has him on edge, because it only occurred to him now that Figstew possibly has omnipresent control over every single one of them. 

Mydei understood that Phainon was intrigued by the idea of meeting someone who’s just as strong as he is, especially when the game has been designed to prop him up as the strongest and most talented person in this universe, destined to defeat every opponent thrown at him.

He can’t, however, understand why he’s constantly pestering him to partake in the most pointless competitions. 

Princess, let’s see who can eat the most. 

Princess, I bet I can wake up earlier than you. 

Princess, what did you score on the alchemy exam? It can't be better than mine. 

“I’d happily carry you if you tripped,” Phainon offers, and Mydei is offended that he’s already considered that possibility. Like Mydei would ever. “We’ve already established that I can take on heavier weights yesterday.”

“We did nothing of the sort, the bags of wheat you were carrying were obviously not as full as mine.”

“Aw, don’t be such a sore loser, it doesn’t suit you.”

“You fucking ass–”

“Who is causing so much ruckus?” Anaxa scolds as he rounds the corner of the hallway. His eye darts between the two of them before he heaves a disgruntled sigh. “Ah, it’s just you.”

Mydei is calm, only mildly surprised that they’re not getting properly yelled at, but Phainon looks like he’d just been caught doing something indecent. 

He’s trembling as he explains himself. “I’m sorry professor, I lost track of where I was and–”

“I don’t care,” Anaxa cuts him off, having already mentally exited the conversation. “Carry on as you are. Or don't. Just don't make too much noise.” 

The professor walks off, but Phainon still looks embarrassed, avoiding Mydei’s eyes and not saying a word to him until they arrive at the lecture hall. 

“You guys are late,” Cyrene says as she punches Mydei’s shoulder. It’s like being scolded by an overenergetic puppy.  “I was starting to worry that Princess Mydeimos got hurt again.”

“We would have arrived faster if I took Phainon’s suggestion to race to class seriously,” Mydei replies with a shrug. 

“Hah, I would have happily raced you,” Cyrene tells Phainon, who still looks like he’d just seen a ghost. Mydei begins to wonder whether that reboot is necessary after all. “I was always faster when we were kids, and you’d always cry about it and go tell your mom.”

“I wouldn’t have asked you.” Phainon’s reply is uncharacteristically snippy, but his childhood best friend does not look fazed. “Also, the princess does not need to know this irrelevant information!”

Mydei stifles a laugh imagining a tiny helpless Phainon allowing himself to get bullied by an even tinier Cyrene. He doesn’t sober up to the fact that these childhood memories are all nonexistent.

“I can assure you, it’s very relevant to me.”

Cyrene smirks. “Afraid that you’ll lose, Mr. Deliverer?”

“Cyrene, please don’t say that,” Phainon replies sternly, not a hint of humor in his face. 

Mydei is baffled. Phainon says it to him all the time. He’s said it in front of Cyrene just yesterday, so it’s not like it’s his competitive streak that he’s hiding from his best friend.

“Oh? Alright, it can be your own little thing,” she concedes with a wink, which only makes Phainon look more distraught. 

Weird.

“Your Highness, I’ve noticed that you’ve been training more these days,” Dan Heng stops him after class a few days later. He would usually train with the princess during his route, but they would like, go on runs together. There is no scenario where Mydei engages in actual combat with his suitors. “I really wonder if you’ve become stronger than me.”

It’s a joke. A perfectly neutral statement. Mydei knows that he’s just trying to make conversation. 

“Oh, a princess like me could never hope to match your prowess, Lord Dan Heng,” he replies like the princess would.

Dan Heng smiles. “There is only one way to fi–”

“No!” 

Mydei is startled when Phainon appears at his side like a phantom. It’s a miracle he’s managed to hold a conversation for longer than 30 seconds without him there. 

“Most people lead with a hello,” Mydei says, irritated. 

“Why?” Dan Heng asks. This poor innocent soul, he seems genuinely confused. He doesn't know Phainon has gone rogue and nothing he does makes sense anymore. 

Phainon stands there for a moment, buffering. He must not have not thought this through at all. 

“Your spear,” is what he finally lands on. “I broke it.”

“You did what?”

“When did you even have the time to–”

“And I’m paying Okhema’s best blacksmith to make it as good as new,” he elaborates impatiently, like they’re distracting from the relevant topic at hand. “You can't spar with His Highness.”

“It was merely a joke,” Dan Heng says, furrowing his eyebrows. “I wouldn't seriously attempt to face the Princess of Castrum Kremnos in battle.”

Who in their right mind would do such a thing? 

The implication hangs awkwardly in the air, and it takes Mydei every ounce of willpower not to quip I know one guy who would do just that and then watch the Deliverer squirm. 

“Princess,” Phainon says sheepishly once Dan Heng is gone. He looks like a kicked puppy, which is kind of ridiculous considering he’s the perpetrator. “I have something important to tell you.”

“Well, obviously. You better explain what the fuck this was just now.” 

“You can't spar or compete with anyone but me, okay?” Mydei looks unimpressed by this request, so he sighs and adds a pathetic, desperate, “Please.” 

Mydei wasn't planning to do that anyway. In the eyes of everyone else in Amphoreus, he’s still the prim and shy princess. “Why should I listen to you?”

Phainon doesn't answer, only stares at his hands as crimson spreads across neck and face. It’s clearly something important to him, because he’s refusing to just spit it out. 

All the dots connect for Mydei then. 

The incessant invitations to compete, looking flustered when he was confronted by their professor, becoming agitated when friends so much as joked about joining in their little games. 

Phainon was flirting with him. 

It’s nothing like the charming, perfectly polished lines that Mydei had come to expect. It’s childish and clumsy and honestly a little stupid, but that's what makes it all the more sincere. 

He was actually, genuinely trying, for the first time in his life. Just to earn Mydei’s attention. 

Mydei wants to grab his face and kiss him senseless. 

“I’ll consider it,” he says instead, rolling his eyes.

Phainon smiles like Mydei just handed him the world.

Year 3. Spring 44. Entry Hour.

╰── ⋅ ⋅ ── ✩ ── ⋅ ⋅ ──╯

“Princess, let’s go on a date this weekend.”

“No?” Mydei tries. He would be lying if he said that he didn't derive a little bit of joy out of making the Deliverer beg for it every time.

The past week has been a confusing blur for Mydei. The affection meter has been rising without him lifting a finger. It feels like he already won the game, and can now sit back and let the days play out until his ticket home is secured. 

It’s a little ironic, Mydei thinks, how his romantic adventure in another world had mellowed down to mirror the boring monotone routine of his normal life. 

Train. Go to class. Spend time with Phainon. 

Is this what his mysterious captors had intended? A corny message about the importance of being yourself?

Phainon might not be real, but the hurt he inflicted on Mydei still stings to this day. As much as Mydei tries not to let his feelings tangle with this simulated world, the vulnerable core of his heart that yearned to be seen and loved would not allow him to brush off Phainon’s initial betrayal and rejection. 

The only excitement he does allow himself is when he’s testing the limits of how mean he can be to Phainon. 

Phainon looks to his left and right. There is no one else in the academy courtyard this early in the morning. 

“Your Highness, do you know what the humble farmboy from Aedes Elysiae said to Lady Aglaea when she told him that he was destined to be Okhema’s Deliverer?”

What the fuck is he on about now? This is exactly why Mydei continues to keep him at an arm’s length. He can never predict what Phainon will say next. 

“What?”

“Deliverer? I hardly know her!” 

Mydei is stunned at first, and it takes him an entire minute to process that Phainon was telling him a joke, and a terrible one at that. 

Then, despite every instinct screaming at him not to, he cracks a tiny smile. 

“Pretty.” The word spills out of Phainon’s mouth so naturally, like’s marveling to himself. 

“What was that for?” Mydei asks, unable to wipe it off his face. 

“You hadn't smiled in a while, and I wanted to see it.”

Mydei blinks. He’s been so caught up in his own feelings of alienation that he hadn't realized Phainon was perfectly attuned to them. In his mind, he convinced himself to process Phainon’s newfound affection as a nonsensical, shallow fixation. 

“In return for making you laugh, will you join me for a picnic this saturday?” Phainon tilts his head cutely.

How is Mydei ever supposed to say no to that? 

“Fine.”

Picnic dates sit at the top of the Legend of Amphoreus intimacy rankings. They can only be activated when the suitor’s affection level is high. 

Despite Phainon’s change of heart, he seems to understand the significance of his invitation, because Mydei is dumbfounded when he arrives in the secluded corner he reserved for them at Okhema’s botanical gardens Saturday afternoon. 

The Deliverer has put together an elaborate setup. A parasol to protect him from the sun, a mountain of cushions, freshly plucked flowers in an ornate vase, and all his favorite Amphoreus treats, with a distinct color palette unifying it all together.

Yellow and purple. 

“What do you think?” Phainon asks. He takes Mydei’s hand to help him sit down, and Mydei immediately notices that he’s trembling under his touch. 

He’s not boasting or fishing for praise with his question. Phainon is genuinely nervous about how Mydei would receive his effort. 

Even with hundreds of virtual dates under his belt, Mydei finds this entirely unfamiliar. He’s used to Phainon confidently sweeping him off his feet, leaving the protagonist to be the one all flustered and nervous instead. 

The effort is all in the details, Mydei’s supposed favorite colors, his favorite food, his favorite flowers. Him. Not the princess. 

Try not to swoon challenge level: Impossible. Mydei has miserably failed.

“You look so happy lately, princess,” Castorice’s soft voice drags him back to reality. 

They’re in the middle of their biweekly book club meeting at the dormitory common room, which Mydei admittedly had been slacking off of attending. Though in his defense, he had a lot on his plate. 

Well yes, because Phainon seems physically incapable of leaving me alone, Mydei thinks.

The game’s characters are set on the paths they choose at the start of the game, which means that Phainon is not able to join him for club meetings no matter how much he would like to. Out of the four suitors, he’s the only one who doesn't get to participate in club activities because his designated interest is the Okhema military. 

What a suffocating existence, to have your entire life mapped out for you from the age of nineteen.

“Is it that obvious?” Mydei asks, feeling his cheek with the back of his hand self-consciously.

“You were humming to yourself while reading,” March agrees. She’s Nice March today, which Mydei is grateful for because he can't face Evil March after giving in to Phainon instead of stabbing him like she advised. 

“Oh, that.” Mydei was humming the game’s idle music. It still feels odd to be in these locations without hearing it playing in the background. “The book’s story reminded me of an old Kremnoan ballad.”

He hadn't had the chance to read fiction books since starting grad school, and club president Castorice’s affinity for heroic tales involving magic and dragons were a nice change of pace.

This month’s book is The Sun is Set to Die, a tragedy about a hero trapped in an endless cycle of death and reincarnation as he tries and fails to save the world. 

Mydei finds it impressive that the game’s developers have inserted entire fleshed out novels for him to read, with grand plots that are seemingly divorced from the cozy and relatively low stakes world of Amphoreus. He had assumed that there was nothing more beyond the book summaries that flashed on the screen whenever he chose the club activity. Perhaps one of the writers was using this as a creative outlet after having to write countless cheesy lines for the game. 

Regardless of the reason, he’s been enjoying this book because the protagonist Khaslana, with his selfless nature and single-minded obsession, reminds him of Phainon. It made it easier for him to become attached to the story and care about what happens to Khaslana, but it also makes all the emotional beats hit so much harder than they normally would.

He’s grateful Phainon winded up here, sentenced to be loved by all and spend his days wooing a princess, and not in that writer’s deeply fucked up world. 

Castorice’s eyes light up. “This one is my favorite, I’m happy that you’ve taken a liking to it as well.”

This is just like her, the more tragic a book is the more excited she gets. It’s such a contrast to her soft and gentle disposition, and Mydei finds it endearing. 

“You guys seem to be having fun,” Phainon says, barging in on their meeting. His tone is lighthearted, but there’s a restless energy to him that Mydei recognizes after spending so much time together. 

Wait, what? Mydei was sure it wasn’t possible for Phainon to join in any activities outside of his set path. 

“How are you in here?” he asks sincerely, and it takes him a second to realize how rude he comes off to everyone at the table. 

“I’m allowed inside the common room, at least last time I checked,” Phainon responds with a smile, relaxing upon hearing the familiar comfort of Mydei’s blunt greeting. 

Mydei supposes that that’s true. It’s not like there are any rules or mentions of the other characters being present in the same place as him, just living their own lives in the background.

Still, he suspects that Phainon did not wind up here by pure chance. 

“No no, I was just asking because I didn’t think that you would be interested in the books we read here,” he says, and Phainon’s eyes narrow, unsure of where he’s going with this. “The romantic subplot in The Sun is Set to Die is quite minor, after all.”

All the blood drains from Phainon’s face, and Mydei bites back a smile. He doesn’t need to know that Mydei is entranced by that exact subplot, the story of Khaslana’s enduring love for the warrior king he once called his rival. 

“Princess, I thought my reading preferences were meant to stay between us,” he hisses, and Mydei rolls his eyes and shrugs. 

“There is no shame in enjoying different genres, we’re still united by our shared love for reading!” Castorice interjects. She’s just excited to have more people to share her favorite stories with. “And if I may offer my own interpretation, I wouldn’t say the romance subplot is minor. The protagonist and his love interest’s rivalry on the battlefield forms the emotional core of the story.” 

Phainon peers down at Mydei with a knowing smile. “Rivalry on the battlefield? That’s very interesting.” 

She nods excitedly, innocently clueless of the source of Phainon’s sudden interest. “The princess has been devouring this book, so you can take his word for it!”

Castorice’s enthusiasm is not so endearing anymore.

“It has a few explicit scenes as well,” March nods. All his friends are filthy traitors. She cranes her neck to sneak a look at Mydei’s book, who is too slow to slam it shut before she can recognize the scene he was on. “Oh, on the exact page His Highness is reading right now.”

Phainon whistles and raises his eyebrows. “Ooh, how scandalous.” 

Yeah. Okay. Fine. It wasn’t just the tragedy or Khaslana’s character that were enticing to him, but it’s been several weeks of being edged by Phainon at this point and his imagination can only take him so far. 

He dons a tight smile and looks up at Phainon. “Yeah, it’s perfect for holding the attention of readers like yourself.” 

“You seem to be the expert,” Phainon deflects his attempt at payback with ease. “So I’ll take your word for it, Your Highness.” 

“Yeah, you should do that.”

“I think I will!”

Castorice clears her throat, and Mydei realizes that they’ve hijacked the meeting with their incessant bickering. He can’t find it in him to feel embarrassed, though, because his chest feels a lot lighter with Phainon around. The only thing missing is their fight turning physical or Phainon taking hold of his hand or waist before resuming the childish teasing. 

Oh Aeons, he’s developed a chronic case of Phainon Deficiency Syndrome. 

“My apologies,” he tells Castorice anyway, and she shakes her head at him. 

“It’s alright, it’s on me for keeping you away from Lord Phainon for so long.”

“An hour and twenty three minutes,” Phainon elaborates before Mydei even gets a chance to pretend that she’s exaggerating the extent of their codependency. “Uhm…or something. I think.”

Mydei was right to be suspicious earlier, Phainon was sitting somewhere, counting down the seconds before he lost his patience and barged in on the single activity he was doing without him that day.

“Which happens to be nearly all the time we have for today, anyway,” she says, closing her book. “Thank you all for joining me today, I’ll see you in two weeks so we can discuss the ending!”

Phainon shifts his weight and drums the back of Mydei’s chair restlessly. “What are you doing after this, princess?”

“I’ll head to the baths, I guess.” 

“Oh! I’ll come with,” Phainon offers without missing a beat.

It’s unfortunately Phainon’s default response to anything that Mydei says. Mydei’s not even sure he actually processed the words that came out of his mouth.

He scans the table, but everyone stares in different directions, wisely refusing to take part in this exchange. 

They stare at each other, Mydei growing more irritated while Phainon maintains innocent confusion. 

“Are you joking, Lord Phainon?” Mydei mercifully gives him an out.

“I’m…not?”  Phainon doesn’t take it, and only belatedly registers that this is a My Wife is Mad at Me and I Must Die situation. “Would you prefer if I was?”

“Look at my face and find the answer yourself,” Mydei flutters his eyelashes at him, and Phainon is momentarily lost in Mydei’s golden eyes before coming to his senses. 

“Of course I’m just joking, Your Highness.” His loyal puppy falls in line, and Mydei rewards him with a whispered good under his breath.

Later on, as they’re packing their things and leaving, Mydei catches murmurs of married couple and well-trained from the other club members. 

He loves being Phainon’s Mydei.

Year 3. Summer 21. Action Hour.

╰── ⋅ ⋅ ── ✩ ── ⋅ ⋅ ──╯

The Saturday before the exhibition match, Phainon and Mydei spend the entire day preparing at the training grounds. 

“There is something on your mind,” Mydei says as Phainon collapses to the ground in a declaration of defeat. 

Phainon, whose been oddly quiet the entire day, brightens up just a bit.  “Am I that easy to read?”

Quite the opposite, actually. If only Phainon knew how much Mydei has suffered trying to peer behind those blue eyes. 

“You haven’t said something stupid like let’s see who can throw the most punches,” Mydei explains, because I know you better than anyone in this world still feels a tad bit too intimate. “Come on, you're due for a break.”

They huddle on the floor together, and Mydei takes out an assortment of snacks from his bag. 

Phainon gasps and covers his mouth, immediately recognizing that they weren't prepared by the academy's kitchen staff.

“I wanted to make up for last time,” Mydei explains as he pushes them in Phainon’s direction. “And because I knew you would be too occupied with your training to remember to eat.”

Phainon looks at him with stars in his eyes, and Mydei can practically hear the single word on his mind before he says it. 

My wife, he mouths as he takes Mydei’s hand and brings it to his lips.

Despite it being abundantly clear that their feelings for each other are mutual, and all the time they have alone, Phainon and Mydei haven't made any progress in terms of physical affection. Mydei thinks it’s mostly the upcoming match taking up most of Phainon’s energy that’s to blame, and he’s just about ready to march into Castrum Kremnos and take the opponent out himself. 

“Aren't you going to make me tell you what’s been on my mind?” Phainon asks once the food returns a semblance of life into his body. 

Mydei shrugs. “You're going to tell me when you’re ready to.”

Of course he’s curious, of course he’s dying to know every little thought inside Phainon’s pretty head, but Mydei also trusts Phainon enough to feel assured that he’s going to tell him eventually.

It’s a new form of intimacy that Mydei has never experienced before. In truth, he didn't even think it could be possible. 

Phainon appears shellshocked by his answer, and he chews his food silently, basking in the space and boundaries Mydei has drawn for him. It occurs to Mydei that he might have never been offered this level of agency in his life. 

“When I was growing up in the village,” he begins as he swallows his last bite, and Mydei sits up straight to give him his full attention. “Our neighbor had a big fluffy white dog. Cyrene and I played with him every day when he was a puppy, and he always had so much energy, running towards us when we called him by the name we came up with together. Snowy.”

He’s smiling to himself as he talks, childish wonder painting over his handsome features. Mydei doesn't know where he’s going with this, but he hangs over every word breathlessly.

“My memories of that time are hazy, but it feels like it happened overnight. One day we were playing with Snowy, and the next he was put to work to herd the neighbor’s cattle, no longer allowed to waste time chasing around the village kids. I watched him take the exact same set path morning after morning, and perhaps out of petty anger as a result of losing my playmate, couldn't fathom how he could be content living like this.”

“Phainon…”

“But he’s just a dog, right? He was bred for this one singular purpose, probably doesn't even register the resentment that I had been projecting on to him. But I was just a kid, and my childish brain could only think about the freedom and ambitions that this dog didn't even have the chance to want.”

It’s the most he’s ever spoken about his feelings outside of his affection for the princess, and even though they’re masked beneath a metaphor, Mydei follows everything he’s trying to communicate. 

Phainon draws a deep breath, mustering some courage before he arrives at the conclusion. “Do you know what the humble farmboy from Aedes Elysiae actually said to Lady Aglaea when she told him that he was destined to be Okhema’s Deliverer?”

Mydei snorts at the callback, which in turn makes Phainon laugh too. As silly as it was, that was the first time that his resolve to keep Phainon at a distance was seriously shaken, and Mydei has never felt more grateful for it.

“What did he say?” 

“He said nothing, because he was told, not asked,” Phainon says, years of service wearing him down to weary submission. “I’ve always been told, I’m always supposed to. Supposed to get entangled in Okheman politics, supposed to become the strongest warrior in my generation, supposed to graduate from the most elite academy, supposed to love…”

He cuts himself off, seemingly afraid that he’s said too much, definitely afraid that Mydei has caught on to what he was going to say next. 

Supposed to love the Kremnoan princess.

Mydei doesn't mind, he wants to know everything. “Tell me, Phainon.”

“Never mind.” Phainon shakes his head, beginning to clamp up again. “I’m sorry, you must think I’m an ungrateful brat. Lady Aglaea is kind, I know she genuinely cares for me, and she provided me with a life beyond my wildest dreams. I don't blame her, or anyone for having expectations for me, because it feels like we’re all cogs in the same machine.” 

“I don't think you’re ungrateful.” Mydei folds his arms. “In fact, I think you’re offering everyone far too much grace and understanding, and leaving nearly none for yourself.”

Phainon looks confused again, like he doesn't know how to react to someone recognizing his personhood. “But I’m the perfect Deliverer, aren't I?” 

Mydei scoffs. “You’re not perfect. You like to run your mouth, you’re far too snarky for your own good, you’re jealous and possessive, you have an obsessive personality, and you do a poor job of masking your dirty thoughts.”

Phainon also has a smile that rivals the sun, he’s selfless and kind, he’s a safe and protective presence. Mydei doesn't have to tell him these things though, it’s all Phainon gets to hear. He’s never been allowed to be anything else, or at least that’s what he’s led himself to believe. 

“Phainon, you’re human.”

I wish you were. 

He might also be the first person to ever look so receptive to someone listing out their flaws as a form of comfort, because his smile grew bigger the more Mydei rattled on. 

“You know, I had become so numb to it all, going through the motions and performing the role expected of me so perfectly that the line between Phainon and the Deliverer had blurred beyond recognition. It was all that I was, performing my life rather than living it,” Phainon says before taking Mydei’s hand and dragging it to his lap. “That is, until a certain princess attempted to kill me.”

It all begins to make sense now. Mydei was the first anomaly, the first disruptive force to ever pierce through the dull harmony of Phainon’s life. A spark of life in an artificial world. 

“You say such things, and then try to convince me that you’re perfect,” Mydei rolls his eyes fondly, and Phainon chuckles. 

“See, this is exactly why I’m irrevocably drawn to you!” Add the ability to say the most heart wrenching things without hesitation to the list of Phainon’s flaws. “Being with you is always exciting, Mydei. You challenge me, frustrate me, help me discover feelings I didn't know I was allowed to have. You make me feel alive.”

The last word pierces through Mydei’s heart like a sharp dagger, and he’s overwhelmed with a mixture of conflicting emotions, torn between the simple beauty of Phainon’s love confession, and the sobering reality that it can never become true. 

“Didn't you think that I don't like you?” Mydei asks, still unsure of how Phainon was able to take his rejections in stride. “Or that I had suddenly started to dislike you?” 

“Of course you like me, Mydei,” Phainon answers without hesitation, and his unwavering trust only deepens the wound. “No one understands you like I do, no one gets to see all sides of you like I do. And besides…”

It should be humiliating, the way Mydei can't disagree with any of Phainon’s bold proclamations, but instead he just feels…seen. “Besides?” 

Phainon’s voice drops to a whisper. “I might be a bit sheltered, but I recognize the way you look at me, princess.” 

Mydei feels a throb between his legs, happy tingles awakening desire through his body. It’s what he deserves for tacking on that dirty thoughts comment earlier. 

With excruciating difficulty, he reels himself back and remembers where they are. Phainon can't afford to have distractions from his match tomorrow, and they're still technically in a public space. That will have to wait for now. 

Mydei leans in to plant a soft kiss on Phainon’s cheek. “How about this Deliverer, regardless of whether you win or lose tomorrow, I’ll grant you one wish.”

“If it doesn’t matter, why not just give it to me now?” Phainon asks, deploying his lethal puppy eyes. He grabs Mydei’s wrist to keep him in place, not satisfied with an innocent peck. 

His impatience really isn’t helping at all. 

“I’m giving you time to think of something good.” Mydei reasons. “You’re not used to wanting things for yourself, are you?”

“I’m starting to learn how to do just that, I think,” Phainon replies as he rubs his thumb over Mydei’s wrist, tracing his veins. 

His desire remains unspoken, echoing faintly in the charged silence between them, and Mydei doesn’t need to hear it to know exactly what it is that Phainon is after.

Phainon releases him. “Tell you what, I’ll come find you after I win, somewhere far away from everyone else.” 

“But you can’t,” Mydei says, in the most literal sense. His path for that day is already pre-written. He’ll wave to the princess in the crowd before being ushered away for interviews, private meetings with the government officials in attendance, and a banquet dinner in his honor at Aglaea’s palace. It’s a rigid schedule that he can't break, because if he could he would have already followed Mydei everywhere regardless of the game’s restrictions. “I mean, you would probably be too busy tomorrow, so let’s just–”

“Mydei,” Phainon cuts him off sharply, and Mydei realizes that he doesn't appreciate the princess dictating what he can or can't do. “I’m going to find you tomorrow.”

Call it delusion, or love rendering him blind to reason. 

Because in that moment, Mydei chooses to believe.

Year 3. Summer 22. Ascent Hour.

╰── ⋅ ⋅ ── ✩ ── ⋅ ⋅ ──╯

It takes two minutes for Phainon’s opponent to fall to his knees and concede defeat.

That man is a beast, Hephaestion would tell Mydei’s father later. Phainon’s sheer bruteness has the crowd silent at first, and a mixture of fear and admiration fills the air as the future that Lady Aglaea promised him all these years ago is now set in stone. 

Mydei is waiting for him somewhere far and secluded as promised, under that ancient tree where Cyrene read their fates. He took off in the midst of the deafening cheers and applause, catching a glimpse of Phainon searching for him in the crowd. 

Ten minutes pass, then fifteen, and he begins to feel silly for believing Phainon could shatter the shackles of this virtual world, the shackles he was born into, just for the sake of the promise he made to Mydei. 

He’s not angry or even disappointed. If anything, he’s already received more than he had ever hoped for when he arrived in Amphoreus, a flawed, complex, breathtakingly human version of the man he loved behind a screen. 

Besides, it's not like this is the only time he can grant Phainon his wish. There's always tomo–

“Told you I’d make it!” Phainon yells out behind him, and Mydei turns to him so fast he nearly trips and lands on his face. 

This bastard actually fucking did it against all odds. He defied the laws of the universe, and is now standing triumphant before Mydei. 

He’s sweating, not from his battle but because he sprinted here from the arena. His white hair is messy, dirt stains his handsome face, and his blue eyes are alert and slightly manic. 

Phainon has been unleashed. 

“I didn’t have to think about it at all, Mydei,” he says breathlessly, and his hands are on Mydei’s waist in an instant. He backs him up against the tree. “I know exactly what it is that I want.”

“Let me hear it,” Mydei whispers as he happily allows Phainon to manhandle him, already feeling lightheaded. 

“You, princess. You’re my first and only selfish desire.”

Tears sting Mydei’s eyes, and he’s rendered speechless in Phainon’s tight, suffocating embrace. Phainon didn't just want him, it’s through Mydei that he learned what it feels like to want at all. 

It’s evident in Phainon’s shallow breathing, in the clumsy, entirely too rough grip he has on Mydei’s waist, in the small grunt he chokes out when Mydei throws his arms over his broad shoulders to drag him closer and press their equally chiseled bodies against each other. 

He’s draped in an elegant, but still revealing gold chiton in a quiet show of support for Okhema’s champion. The fabric glimmers under the afternoon sun, perfectly wrapping around Mydei’s body in all the right places and drawing attention to his hefty chest with its deep v-neckline. 

Phainon doesn't kiss him immediately, he breathes Mydei in, inhaling and releasing hot puffs of air into his neck, under his ears, and over his jaw, as his whole body trembles like it’s about to collapse. 

Mydei closes his eyes and whimpers. He’s never felt so wanted. 

It takes him a moment to remember that this is Phainon’s first time doing anything like this, as he’s spent his entire adult life in celibacy waiting on the princess. He might need a little bit of guidance.

Mydei tilts his head back and catches Phainon’s sharp jaw between his fingers. Phainon stares at him in confusion, in utter reverence and worship, but remains still and obedient. 

The first taste of Phainon’s lips elicits a satisfied, low moan at the back of Mydei’s throat. Despite it being their first time, it doesn't take long for their mouths to slot together perfectly, and Mydei wastes no time opening his mouth to deepen the kiss, encouraging Phainon to let loose and act on his desires with a steady string of whimpers. He’s not usually this loud, but the way Phainon shudders and grunts every time he hears his voice is simply too addicting.

Of course, this pales in comparison to the other reason, which is that Phainon feels good. His weight crashing against Mydei’s, the last remnants of chivalry and restraint rapidly crumbling to temptation. 

“Was it everything you had hoped for?” Mydei asks as he catches his breath, arrogance coloring his voice. He knows he’s a good kisser. 

He didn't mean for his question to be taken as a provocation, just a poorly masked attempt to fish for compliments. What Mydei failed to consider is just how far Phainon’s childish competitive streak extends.

The Deliverer doesn't answer. Instead, he locks Mydei’s eyes with his as he pushes away the shimmering fabric of Mydei’s neckline to cup his breast. His hands are gruff and sweaty, but just big enough to eclipse Mydei’s pecs. He gives it an experimental squeeze, and is rewarded with a small, adorable moan that Mydei miserably fails to restrain. 

He sticks his tongue out before shoving it back into Mydei’s mouth, allowing Mydei to suck on it while his hand pulses over his chest, applying more pressure as the princess melts further and further under his touch.

They break apart with a trail of saliva. Mydei’s face is flushed, his nipples are stiff and perky, and his panties have been utterly destroyed. 

Phainon lazily swipes a finger over Mydei’s glossy, bruised lips, eyes half lidded and dark. 

“I’m not so sure yet, princess,” he answers the question Mydei had forgotten he even asked. “I think we need to do some additional testing.”

Mydei’s heart catches in his throat, feeling defenseless against the newly awakened, insatiable Deliverer.

Year 3. Summer 25. Parting Hour.

╰── ⋅ ⋅ ── ✩ ── ⋅ ⋅ ──╯

Once Phainon has a taste, he becomes impossible to satiate.

“Please, princess,” he whines, face buried in Mydei’s neck. “Just a moment more.”

“You have to wake up early for training tomorrow, you idiot,” Mydei chastises as he cards his fingers through Phainon’s hair. “We’ll see each other again afterwards.”

“I’m missing you already,” Phainon insists. “Especially because…”

Phainon has Mydei backed up against the door of his dorm. It’s the end of the day, and he’s kissing him like it’s the last time they’ll ever see each other.

“Especially because, what?”

His question is what finally distracts Phainon from his mission to paint Mydei’s neck in red. 

“You didn't forget, did you?” he asks, and Mydei shrugs in confusion. “The two week summer holiday begins in just a few days.” 

Mydei’s heart sinks. “Oh.” 

He did forget, but for a very understandable reason. The two week period spent away from school is timeskipped through a little animation of the princess sleeping in the imperial palace of Castrum Kremnos. 

And he’s been so wrapped up in making up for the seemingly endless weeks of pent up sexual frustration that he’s neglected checking the calendar. 

(Perhaps he’s also chosen to avoid acknowledging the passage of time because he knows it’s not in his favor.) 

He looks at Phainon, who’s looking down in deep contemplation, and it goes on long enough for Mydei to begin to wonder whether he’s just lost himself staring at his cleavage. 

“I’ve actually been thinking about something…” Phainon trails off, uncertain. 

“You know you can tell me anything,” Mydei reassures him flatly. 

Phainon clenches his fist and psyches himself up. “I want you to come spend the holiday with me at Lady Aglaea’s,” he blurts out in one breath, as though he would lose his courage if he paused for even a second. 

A million rejections rush to Mydei’s mind at once. The system won’t allow it. Figstew is here, and I think I’m shackled to it. Does Aglaea’s palace even exist as a location if the princess has never been there before?
