It’s the last night before they have to return to the academy.

Phainon left his bedroom sometime ago, and Mydei hasn't gotten a wink of sleep since. 

The past two weeks have been an escape from the system. For the first time since he arrived in Amphoreus, Mydei truly felt like an inhabitant rather than a captive or an alien invader, walking on eggshells to avoid disrupting the flow of this fairytale world. 

But tomorrow, he has to face reality, he has to come to terms with the fact that he has to say goodbye to Phainon someday.

He has to look at that percentage again. 

Mydei has been able to ignore the inevitable for as long as he has because Phainon is simply too human, too flawed, too loving to be nothing but lines of code. 

With a million thoughts weighing too heavy on his mind, Mydei throws on his robe and decides to take a walk to clear his head and maybe tire him enough to fall asleep. 

The hallways of Aglaea’s palace are even more confusing in the dark, and he isn't any better at navigating them now than at the start of his summer vacation. Mydei takes two left turns, then pivots right, and soon finds himself in completely unfamiliar surroundings. 

Perfect. Now he has to find his way back to his room or risk having to sleep on the floor. 

He sighs and leans on the wall, sliding down until he’s crouching on his knees. Could the developers have made this place any less welcoming? 

Then, amidst the all-encompassing darkness and silence, Mydei hears a door creak, and a faint light at the end of the hallway. 

Oh thank Aeons, he’s been saved. One of the servants must still be up, and they’ll surely be able to help him back to his room. 

He follows the source of light, but his frantic steps slow when he recognizes the door that it’s coming from. 

It’s Aglaea’s office. 

He hasn't seen her in days, and thus assumed she was away on some important business again. Would she be angry at him for sneaking around in the middle of night, or suspect the innocence of his intentions? It’s difficult to explain that he got lost in the place he’s been staying at for the past two weeks. 

Mydei shakes his head. What’s wrong with him? What could Aglaea possibly do to him? She’s literally an NPC. 

With an uneasy feeling at the pit of his stomach, Mydei steps into the light. 

What greets him isn't an angry Aglaea, or a helpful servant. 

It’s Professor Anaxa, studying a projection of a chart that Mydei has seen a hundred times, but with a few crucial changes.  

┌───────── ⋆⋅☆⋅⋆ ─────────┐

Subject NeiKos496

Human Development Progress 

████████████▒ 95%

└───────── ⋆⋅☆⋅⋆ ─────────┘

Behind him, the large board of golden threads has changed, too. The pieces of parchment are no longer blank, they display fragmented images of his time in Amphoreus thus far. 

This is a control room. 

“Oh, it’s you,” the professor greets with an unenthusiastic wave. 

“What is the meaning of this?” Mydei asks, folding his arms and sticking to the door. Is his sleep deprived mind playing tricks on him? 

“I’m working overtime, that’s what,” Anaxa answers, like it’s Mydei’s fault. “This isn’t even a part of my job description, you know? But the esteemed Lady Aglaea has roped me into fixing plot holes left and right while she’s busy maintaining the stability of the simulation. Honestly, Madam Herta owes me a fat raise along with a lifetime supply of droma merchandise.” 

“That’s not what I meant,” Mydei cuts him off, then he furrows his eyebrows. “....Did you just say Herta?” 

As in, Genius Society Herta? Mydei is distantly aware of her and her genius peers, as they sometimes collaborate with his university for research projects. 

Anaxa stares at him. “Mydeimos. You should sit down before I explain everything to you, because if you faint it will be my mess to clean up.” 

“I don't trust you,” Mydei replies flatly. How is he meant to know for sure that Anaxa, Herta, and whoever else haven't entered this world with ill intentions? 

What if they put Phainon in danger?

It’s as if Anaxa can read his mind. “Phainon is fine. His wellbeing is as much of a priority for us as it is for you.”

Mydei thinks back to all their run-ins with the professor. He’s always been a tad too eccentric, meaning that he hasn’t been an NPC at any point in time since Mydei arrived. If he wanted to harm either of them in any way, he would have done so by now.

So he sits down, his guard still up, as the mysterious projection looms over him menacingly.

“Approximately 3000 years ago, a desperate mother was living on a planet facing imminent extinction,” Anaxa explains. “She knew there was no hope left for her home and its inhabitants, but she still yearned to ensure the survival of her only son. His flame couldn't be extinguished so soon after he was born.”

The professor uses a palm sized command panel to manipulate the projection, warping it from the meter to an image of a blue and gold crystal. 

“In her home, devices known as Coreflames were used to store data. Books, letters, images. What it was never used for, however, was storing a soul, sentient life,” he continues. “It’s a shame that such a great feat of alchemy was nearly lost to time.”

Mydei feels a lump in his throat. He has an inkling of where Aanxa’s story was headed.

“But it wasn’t,” he says.

“Correct,” Anaxa replies. “The Coreflame drifted for centuries before miraculously landing in the hands of two Genius Society members, the only ones who could decipher the true nature of the device. But this was only half of the battle. Discovering the existence of the soul was easy, but restoring it to a full-fledged sentient being was a great effort requiring years of research, a full team of the universe’s greatest minds, a virtual incubator in the form of, say, a dating sim, and of course, a few unwitting playtest participants.”

He stares at Mydei pointedly. 

“How many, exactly?” he asks through gritted teeth. 

“33 million, give or take,” Anaxa shrugs. 

Mydei feels like he’s going to be sick. Phainon had to live out this life 33 million times, all for the sake of satisfying an academic curiosity. 

“And for what reason?”

“The reason is what stumped us and stalled our research for months. He had grown from corrupted strings of data to a fully grown human inside the simulation, but he still wasn't alive, not really. There was one missing variable, one that was really obvious in hindsight,” Anaxa’s cold demeanor softens just for a moment. “Do you still remember your objective, Mydeimos?” 

Of course Mydei remembers. The objective that had put him through unspeakable anguish at the start now pokes at the back of his mind like a shameful secret. 

He thinks of the meter Anaxa was studying just now, of how it mirrors his own. 

The answer is so simple. 

“It’s to make him feel love.”

Anaxa smiles gently, and Mydei thinks he sees a glimmer of pride. “It makes sense, doesn't it? Phainon exists today because of someone’s love, and it’s another person’s love that will set him free.”

It’s the first time that Anaxa had said his name, acknowledged that Phainon is alive and real, that he’s not confined to a video game world forever. 

Mydei has only cried in front of two people throughout his adult life. The first was his mother, and the second was Phainon. 

This wasn't about to change tonight. He blinks back the tears forming in his eyes, and swallows the sob bubbling in his throat. 

“Should you be telling me all this?” Mydei asks, because it all feels too good to be true. Maybe Anaxa is selling him a lie before taking him out for good. 

He’s scared, because he thinks that even that would be a happier ending for him than one where he’s separated from Phainon. 

“It doesn't matter, Mydeimos. You’ve already succeeded. We’re at the endgame now,” Anaxa waves him off. “I’ll allow you a few more questions before I make you get the hell out of here. We’ll call it rapid fire exposition.”

That's a little on the nose, but whatever. 

“Why did you make this elaborate dating simulator scheme instead of forming relationships with him yourselves?”

“It compromised the integrity of the research, which also happened to be the reason why we kept you in the dark thus far, and why we wipe the memories of every failed playtester,” he answers dryly. “That didn't stop us from developing genuine care for him, though. As crude as you might think our methods might be.”

“And you had to sell a video game to find test subjects?”

“Growing a human isn't free, kid. We had to make money somehow.”

Well, at least the stupid amount of money he dumped on Phainon merchandise hasn't fully gone to waste. 

“Is every NPC also…?”

“No. Many of the characters, including ones that you’re very familiar with, are in-game avatars of the team that can be possessed at any time to directly observe the subject. Only Cyrene, Aglaea and I have used our avatars around you, as far as I know.”

He thinks back to when Cyrene would tell Phainon things that conveniently moved their relationship along. The chocolate, the flower crown…

“Uh, why are you a love interest?”

Anaxa glares at him. “Do you seriously want to waste a question on something so stupid?” 

“Avoiding the answer only makes me more curious,” Mydei says. He’s too tired to think of much else. 

“Because Aglaea thought it would be funny.”

Mydei’s respect for Aglaea triples. This explains why Anaxa’s route was so devoid of romance. 

“Who is Figstew?”

“Madam Herta made it for you because you seemed to find her voice recording intimidating. She’s still a little offended that you like it more than her, by the way.”

Aeons, he hopes he never runs into her in the real world. 

He scrambles to move on to the next question. “What was the highest percentage that anyone had reached before me?”

The professor scoffs. “Didn't take you to be the jealous type. Believe it or not, ten percent was the highest that anyone had ever achieved across tens of millions of playtests,” he tells him, and Mydei can't fight back the pleased smile that creeps on his lips. “Alright, last one. Better make it good.”

Truthfully, none of the details of the experiment really matter. There was only one question on Mydei’s mind the entire time. Only one thing that will make this all worth it. 

“Can I see Phainon once I return home?”

This gives Anaxa a pause, and his silence immediately makes Mydei regret asking. 

“We were going to tell you this once you met your objective, but I suppose it’s better if you had more time to think about it,” he sighs, and his disclaimer only makes Mydei’s heart sink further. “The truth is that we’re still unsure of whether Phainon’s consciousness can be transferred into a physical form. It could take months, years, and that's if it even works. As you had succeeded in awakening Phainon, the team has decided to leave the choice up to you out of respect.”

He doesn't want to hear it. “No…” 

“You can leave everything behind and live in this simulation with Phainon indefinitely, an immortal life of happiness where the two of you can be together for as long as you’d like,” Anaxa sucks in a breath before he continues. “Or, you can choose to complete the extrapolation and leave the simulation for the uncertain possibility of meeting Phainon out there again, as a human capable of experiencing all the joy and strife that come with being alive.”

Phainon’s fist hovers over the door. 

He agreed to meet with the princess today, who should be expecting him any moment now. Perhaps the princess already finished getting ready and is sitting on the other side eagerly, his heart racing and his fingers fidgeting in anticipation.

He, on the other hand, feels absolutely nothing. 

Guilt gnaws away at him as he braces for this date. Phainon has long stopped trying to make sense of the hollow space where his heart should be, but that doesn't stop him from being ashamed of it nonetheless. 

Well, it doesn't matter what he thinks. He makes the princess happy. He makes everyone happy. What more could he hope to achieve?

That’s unusual.

There is no answer, only heavy, unfamiliar footsteps rushing towards him. 

The door flings open, and Phainon loses his breath. 

Mydeimos, the perfect, prim Princess of Castrum Kremnos is standing before him in his night gown. His golden eyes are wild and his blond curls are sticking out in all directions, but that barely distracts Phainon from how revealing the thin gown is, how it hugs his chiseled muscles and leaves nothing to his imagination. 

Has the princess always looked so…tempting?

It’s the end of another perfect date with the princess!

“I was honored to have those few hours of your time to myself, Mydeimos,” Phainon lies with a perfectly practiced bow. “I hope I offered you some comfort during those brief moments we had together.”

I’m a man with a one track mind, always greedy for more.
